title: Green pitcher
summary: In Santa María Atzompa, near Oaxaca, potters shape pitchers, jars and plates by hand and coat them with a green glaze before firing. Leaves, dots and small flowers are painted or printed on the body in cream and dark green. Here you throw a pitcher with a handle and glaze each band.
howToPlay: Look at the lit pitcher in its frame: it shows the shape and the glaze of each band.
Drag across the clay to set how wide each row is.
Press Glaze, then tap a band and a glaze: green, honey or cream.
Press Check to see your stars, or Watch and learn to see a round played for you.
rules: Shape counts for 70 percent of the score: the closer each of the 12 rows is to the width of the lit target, the better.
Finish counts for 30 percent: a band scores when it carries the same swatch as the target.
The handle on the pitcher is part of the picture; the shape counts the body of the pitcher.
Undo takes back one stroke; Reshape goes back to the clay; Reset starts the shape again.
Three stars for 88 or more, two stars for 65 and one star for 40.
heritageNote: Green glazed pottery is a hallmark of Santa María Atzompa, a village on the hills above Oaxaca in southern Mexico. Potters there glaze their pieces with a lead-free green and fire them in wood kilns; sprigs, dots and flowers are added in cream and dark green.
